policy: Shared original-symbol geometry and palette. Both original wording and Oracle wording with original symbols use these defaults; modern symbols and custom frames retain their existing defaults. Original wording is supplied identically to both sides of the native replay and is not integrated by this receipt. Historical scan cohorts are reused, not a fresh holdout. Regional scan metrics are not whole-card accuracy percentages. Release remains grouped.

controlsBaseline.policy: These same 98 controls were byte-identical before the frame integration; the frozen pre-frame baseline therefore also identifies their frame-only baseline.

findings: Source numeral artwork outperforms five tested font alternatives for all three sets. Native mask fits are retained over high-resolution font-proxy offsets.

Native full-cohort checks support the shared shape/number candidates overall. The small control subset alone misrepresented Fourth Edition numeral training performance; full training and reused validation both improve.

Fallen Empires white uses unchanged glyph geometry. Its slight mask-score regression follows a palette change and relative-threshold resampling, not a new sun shape. Dense sun antialiasing biases a bright-cluster source median; native flat-fill mode identifies the exact requested color.

All 18 disc-paper groups improve median Oklab distance on reused validation, but percentile sensitivity is retained and some bright-tail comparisons regress. These are regional diagnostics, not whole-card correctness percentages.

Black historical glyph preparation used a fixed rim probe that darkened requested paper by 10–13 RGB levels. An opaque-percentile sampling probe restores the exact target within one byte on all 25 controls; cost pixel changes remain inside black discs and glyph overlap also improves.
All scans, cohorts and circle coordinates remain frozen. Native replays use historical repeated validation, not a new untouched holdout.
Solid glyph cores use one shared ink RGB per set, fitted only on calibration names and balanced by color, material and distinct name. No thinner or hollow glyph is introduced.

All 113 measurable validation cores improve Oklab distance on 129 native controls. Six thin cores are excluded; two calibration cores regress and remain recorded. Flat disc colors and all unrelated pixels are unchanged.

X uses the existing generic disc and shared ink palette without numeral-size/offset changes. Native before/after isolation passes on all 17 variable-cost records; all flat X discs hit the requested target within one byte. Coverage differences stay below .0011. Two Fourth Edition paper-distance examples regress. X has insufficient exact native solid-core pixels for the strict ink-color diagnostic, so no X ink-distance claim is made.

Fourth Edition Drain Life originally costs {1}{B}; current upstream cost data is {X}{1}{B}. The exact-printing original-wording correction is reviewed against the scan; Oracle data is retained. Earlier development evidence is preserved, not overwritten.

Current mana gallery now includes calibrated ink and retains all controls, regional regressions, aligned scan, transparent overlay, difference and red/green views. Historical validation is reused, not an untouched final holdout.
